title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Earnestly Studying and Correctly Applying the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Diligently Studying and Correctly Applying

the Marriage Law of the PRC

Fa Fa [2001] No. 9

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Amending the Marriage Law of the PRC was adopted at the 21st Session of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress on April 28, 2001, and shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. To ensure the unified and correct implementation of the Marriage Law of the PRC, we hereby notify as follows:

1. Fully recognize the important significance of amending the Marriage Law. The Marriage Law is an important law that concerns the vital interests of every citizen and every family. Since the reform and opening up, along with changes in China's socioeconomic conditions and people's ideological concepts, new situations and new issues have also emerged in marital and family relations. This amendment to the Marriage Law will play a significant role in establishing equal, harmonious, and civilized marital and family relations, maintaining social stability, and promoting the construction of a socialist spiritual civilization and social progress.

2. People's courts at all levels shall organize judicial personnel, especially civil judicial personnel, to diligently study the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Amending the Marriage Law of the PRC adopted at the 21st Session of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress. Various methods shall be used to provide professional training to judicial personnel, link theory with practice, grasp the legislative intent, and correctly understand the legal provisions.

3. As of April 28, 2001, when hearing cases involving marital disputes, people's courts shall uniformly apply the Marriage Law of the PRC as amended at the 21st Session of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress. Laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations that are inconsistent with the amended Marriage Law of the PRC shall no longer be applied in the hearing of first-instance and second-instance marital and family cases.

4. The Supreme People's Court will step up the drafting of relevant judicial interpretations on the basis of investigation and research. In the process of studying and applying the amended Marriage Law of the PRC, people's courts at all levels shall earnestly summarize trial experience, conduct in-depth investigation and research, pay attention to collecting typical cases, and promptly report to this Court any issues concerning the application of law.

May 10, 2001
